text:
The closest explicit recency-sampling precedent is Petrov and Macdonald’s [RSS (RecSys 2022)](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643), later extended with exponential and power importance functions. RSS samples multiple targets with probabilities increasing toward recent positions, removes those items, and predicts the resulting positive set from the remaining sequence using BCE or LambdaRank. Remaining input can include interactions occurring after a sampled target; this is not strict-prefix next-item prediction. Published experiments applied RSS to GRU4Rec, Caser and SASRec, with BERT4Rec as a baseline. Thus, recency-weighted target selection has clear precedent, but those results do not directly establish its effectiveness inside BERT4Rec.

[Original BERT4Rec (2019)](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690) already combines random masked-item reconstruction with additional last-item-only masked examples, and explicitly discusses historical-prefix/next-item samples. Consequently, terminal MASK supervision and prefix sampling alone offer limited novelty. Its reconstruction loss averages negative log-likelihood over masked targets; the paper does not specify the proposed equal, separately normalized reconstruction-plus-terminal objective or fixed 0.1 endpoint mixture. Sliding-window subsequences also predate this proposal, but do not inherently overweight recent target positions: that depends on window and endpoint selection.

The proposed recipe differs operationally: each terminal target sees only its preceding history, while a separate reconstruction task learns bidirectional context. A fixed 0.1 full-history endpoint probability reserves explicit mass for the latest training target; total endpoint probability also depends on whether the other sampling branch can select it. Equal separately normalized losses fix task weighting independently of reconstruction-mask count. These are defensible experimental distinctions, not established novelty. Useful controls within one jointly trained BERT4Rec per category: uniform versus recency-weighted endpoints, endpoint-mixture probability, context-window length, and reconstruction/terminal loss weight, holding training compute fixed.
